caveats: The paper reports Macro-Precision / Macro-Recall / Macro-F1 / AUC in percent, and this project's result files use the same macro averaging ('average': 'macro'), so the aggregation is comparable.

This project's models were trained from the released CSV trajectories with the paper's length filters. The paper does NOT describe its train/validation/test split or its positive/negative pair construction, so the two evaluations are run on different (though similar) sample populations.
The paper prints only five-run averages with no standard deviation; this project reports mean and population standard deviation over the same five seeds (454, 512, 631, 812, 932).
The paper reports no Accuracy; this project's ISP-Weibo summary includes Accuracy, which has no counterpart in Table 2.

The paper also removes sequences shorter than 3 from ISP and Weibo; the released training code contains no such minimum-length filter (the reproduced Weibo index still contains users with a single check-in), so a small number of extremely short trajectories that the paper would have dropped are present here.
The paper's Table 2 'Impro.' row and two claims in the abstract/ablation text are internally inconsistent with its own tables, so the paper numbers are quoted as published and never recomputed.
Differences in F1/AUC below roughly two percentage points cannot be interpreted as a methodological difference given the undocumented split and pair sampling.
